preconditions.description: The number of cities n is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.
The number of roads m is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.
The number of queries q is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.
The length of the building type array T is equal to the number of cities n.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= T[i] <= 10**9 for i in range(n))
preconditions.description: Each building type T[i] is between 1 and 1,000,000,000 inclusive.
The number of roads is equal to m.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= roads[i][0] <= n and 1 <= roads[i][1] <= n and 1 <= roads[i][2] <= 10**9 for i in range(m))
preconditions.description: Each road connects two distinct cities and has a crowd value between 1 and 1,000,000,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(roads[i][0] != roads[i][1] for i in range(m))
preconditions.description: No road connects a city to itself.
The number of queries is equal to q.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= queries[i][0] <= n and 1 <= queries[i][1] <= n and 1 <= queries[i][2] <= n for i in range(q))
preconditions.description: Each query specifies two cities and a minimum number of unique building types between 1 and n inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(result, int) for result in results)
all(result == -1 or (1 <= result <= 10**9) for result in results)
postconditions.description: Each result is either -1 or a crowd value between 1 and 1,000,000,000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(result == -1 or (len(set(T[i] for i in path)) >= queries[j][2]) for j, result in enumerate(results) if result != -1)
postconditions.description: If a result is not -1, the path from x to y has at least k different types of buildings.

postconditions.expression: all(result == -1 or (result == max(u for x, y, u in path_edges) for j, result in enumerate(results) if result != -1)
postconditions.description: If a result is not -1, it is the maximum crowd value of the path from x to y.
